Definition: apparently neuter of a superlative from the same as G730; the best meal (or breakfast; perhaps from ἦρι ("early")), i.e. luncheon:--dinner.
BiblicalUsage: The ariston is the main meal, dinner or breakfast, and Jesus uses it to teach about the kingdom and about hospitality. A king sends servants to call guests to a dinner already prepared, a Pharisee marvels that Jesus sits down to dinner without washing first, and Jesus tells a host not to invite only friends who can repay the meal.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the dinner table is one of Jesus' favourite pictures of the kingdom, because a meal is invitation, provision and fellowship all at once. And I hold that His rule for hosts still stands: invite those who cannot pay you back, and let God be the one who repays.
